# 26. CMS & No-Code Export

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Allow content workflows and no-code exports only when the final site remains portable, static, accessible, and free of proprietary runtime lock-in.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A source-of-truth decision record for content: Markdown, JSON, CSV, Git-based CMS, headless CMS free tier, spreadsheet export, or no-code export.
- [ ] An export policy requiring plain HTML/CSS/JS assets that can be hosted independently.
- [ ] A cleanup checklist for exported markup, unused CSS, inline styles, injected scripts, tracking, and proprietary comments.
- [ ] A content editing workflow that non-developers can use without paid lock-in where required.
- [ ] A backup and migration plan for content and assets.
- [ ] A schema or content model for repeatable content such as posts, projects, services, FAQs, and locations.
- [ ] An accessibility review requirement for generated or exported components.
- [ ] A license and terms review for no-code tools and CMS providers.

## Must Be True
- [ ] The published site must not require a paid builder runtime.
- [ ] Exported code must be editable with ordinary tools and understandable by a developer.
- [ ] Content must be retrievable in standard formats such as Markdown, HTML, JSON, CSV, or media files.
- [ ] Generated markup must be cleaned enough to meet accessibility, performance, SEO, and security standards.
- [ ] The workflow must not trap the client in a tool they cannot leave.
- [ ] CMS free-tier limits must match expected content volume, traffic, roles, and API needs.
- [ ] Client editing permissions must not allow accidental script injection into production pages.
- [ ] No-code convenience must not override source control and launch QA.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check exported HTML for semantic structure, duplicate IDs, missing labels, inline event handlers, and excessive wrappers.
- [ ] Check exported CSS for unused rules, fixed dimensions, inaccessible focus states, and global overrides.
- [ ] Check exported assets for large files, unclear licenses, and broken paths.
- [ ] Check that forms, analytics, embeds, and scripts survive export without proprietary dependencies.
- [ ] Check that content can be backed up and restored without paid account access.
- [ ] Check that generated pages have unique metadata and clean URLs.
- [ ] Check that build or export steps are documented and repeatable.
- [ ] Check provider terms for commercial use, data processing, and export rights.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid no-code tools that only publish through their proprietary hosting when portability is required.
- [ ] Avoid paid plugins for basic SEO, forms, sliders, galleries, or analytics.
- [ ] Avoid editing minified exported files as the long-term source of truth.
- [ ] Avoid unreviewed script blobs injected by builders.
- [ ] Avoid CMS APIs at runtime for static pages unless there is a build-time generation process.
- [ ] Avoid treating generated markup as automatically production-quality.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] Content workflows must serve maintainability, not just initial convenience.
- [ ] Exports must be clean enough to pass the same standards as hand-authored static pages.
- [ ] The client must be able to leave the tool with their content and site intact.
- [ ] No-code must not become no-quality-control.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the audit script after every export to catch structural regressions.
- [ ] Use cleanup reports to decide whether export output is acceptable or needs a proper static rebuild.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Static-first CMS strategy: static site is the source of design truth, complete without CMS, structured for future editing, exportable to WordPress.org, Decap/Git CMS, Markdown/JSON/YAML, or another free/open-source direction without paid builder lock-in.
- [ ] CMS rules cover acceptable directions, avoided paid/proprietary platforms, selection criteria, WordPress export readiness, Git-based CMS readiness, content model, editable sections, page templates, navigation, media library, blog, portfolio/case studies, testimonials, FAQs, SEO fields, accessibility fields, protected design system, no-code editing, maintenance workflow, monitoring, backups/versioning, WordPress maintenance, custom fields, plugins, export mapping, static-to-WordPress, static-to-Decap, governance, roles, security, performance, analytics continuity, migration, red flags, and final approval.
- [ ] Editors can change content, images, CTAs, metadata, FAQs, testimonials, portfolio, contact details, and legal text without destroying layout, accessibility, SEO, performance, or global design rules.
- [ ] CMS export preserves metadata, alt text, schema, redirects, analytics, forms, legal pages, performance, accessibility, responsive behavior, and visual quality.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
